oh_mad_river_gorge_nature_preserve.blurb: Mad River Gorge is a riverside gorge just outside Springfield, Ohio, with cliff bands that rank among the tallest and largest climbing walls in the state. It was a favorite in the 1980s and 1990s and has been cleaned up and brought back into use. Bouldering is the biggest share, followed by sport routes, with a smaller number of trad lines and top-ropes. The routes are mostly short and high quality, with overhanging, pocketed walls, and they cover most grades from about 5.6 to 5.12. Boulder problems range from V0 to V9, mostly in the easy and middle grades. The southern side is the developed part. The cliffs can be climbed year-round, though humidity is a problem in warm weather.

wa_lookout_point_area.blurb: Lookout Point is a cluster of crags beside the town of Index, in the Skykomish Valley of the Central-West Cascades, roughly an hour east of Seattle. Trad dominates, with sport routes, a dozen or so top-ropes, a little aid and a few boulders. Grades center on 5.10, with a good spread of 5.7 to 5.9 and a smaller group of 5.11 and 5.12 climbs. The area offers more moderate lines than much of Index, thanks to low-angle faces, along with crack climbs, corners, steep faces and arêtes. Many routes are multi-pitch. The setting is forested and shady, and slabby sections dry quickly after rain. Lookout Point, Planet Index, Private Idaho and Halloween are the biggest pieces.

va_2_mile_two.blurb: Mile Two is a stretch of Guest River Gorge in southwest Virginia, with sandstone in a gorge setting. Bouldering is the main event, with problems from V0 into the V10 range, and the boulders are regarded as among the best sandstone boulders in the state. Roped climbing is substantial too: sport routes lead the way, backed by a smaller number of trad lines. Routes run from about 5.7 to 5.14, with many in the 5.10 to 5.12 range. It is split between Mile Two Boulders and Mile Two Routes, so a day can mix both styles in one gorge.

nh_cathedral_ledge.blurb: Cathedral Ledge is a granite wall of about 500 feet above North Conway, in the White Mountains, and it is the center of trad climbing in New Hampshire. The cliff faces east, getting morning sun and falling into shade in early afternoon. Trad dominates, with long multi-pitch routes, face climbs and splitter cracks, plus a few sport routes, some aid lines, a small bouldering zone and ice in winter. Grades center on 5.9 to 5.12, with easier multi-pitch routes at the lower end and a handful of 5.13 and harder lines. Barber Wall, Airation Buttress, Mordor Wall and Thin Air Face are among the biggest sections. Fall is the best season, summer can work, and spring often brings seepage.

ca_mount_rubidoux.blurb: Mount Rubidoux is a 161-acre hill covered in boulders, rising above the city of Riverside, California. The rock is light-colored quartz monzonite in slabs and blocks, fairly smooth, with small sharp edges that reward precise footwork. Bouldering dominates, with a good number of top-ropes and a few trad lines. Problems run from very easy up to V11, with most in the V0 to V4 range, which makes it friendly for beginners while still testing experienced climbers. Top-ropes run from easy to about 5.12. Most problems are short with clean landings. The boulders are spread over zones such as Beach, Island, Half Moon and Hardy Boy. The best climbing runs from fall through early spring, while summers are hot with little shade. The hill is shared with walkers and joggers.
